context.situation: Original synthetic paper game: Harbour and Channel choose one signal simultaneously without seeing the other's choice.
context.availability: Both players can choose any named signal in this state; there are no prerequisites or exclusive inventories.
context.horizon: One clash, settled immediately; no later state, learning, geometry or repeated-game incentives are modeled.

utility.meaning: A positive entry transfers that many utility credits from Channel to Harbour; a negative entry reverses the transfer. The paper game's declared preference is linear in these credits.
utility.unit: net utility credits to Harbour per clash
utility.costs: All signals are free to choose. Every modeled gain and loss is the stated transfer; no time, equipment or opportunity cost is omitted within this one-clash model.
